case: Keppel KAP 2026 – Tough Love (PE acquisition of an Australian fitness chain)
assumptions_log: $80m is enterprise value on a cash-free, debt-free basis; the existing debt behind the Year 0 interest is repaid by the vendor.
Entry costs (2% of price) and the 1.5% upfront loan fee are paid at close and funded in Sources & Uses (not expensed in Years 1–5).
Exit costs are 2% of the exit enterprise value.
New capex is depreciated from the year it is spent (full year); existing assets keep $740k a year.
Interest is charged on the opening loan balance (no circularity); the loan amortises straight-line over 5 years.
Tax is 20% of positive profit before tax; no tax losses carried forward.
All free cash flow to equity is paid to the sponsor each year; minimum cash is nil.
WACC weights use the deal's capital structure at close (loan vs sponsor equity); terminal growth 2.5% is our assumption.
alt_method: Trading comparables: pick listed gym / fitness chains (e.g. Viva Leisure, Planet Fitness, The Gym Group, Basic-Fit), tier them by similarity (format, geography, growth).
Take EV / LTM and NTM EBITDA for each, drop outliers, and use the median or interquartile range.
Apply the range to Tough Love's Year 0 / Year 1 EBITDA to get an EV range; cross-check with precedent gym transactions (control premium).
Show the result next to the DCF and the $80m asking price on a football-field chart.
